C0036.title: Fuglede-Putnam theorem
C0036.body:
Let M and N be NORMAL operators on a Hilbert space and let T be a bounded operator with M T = T N. Then also M* T = T N*. Taking M = N gives Fuglede's theorem: an operator commuting with a normal operator also commutes with its adjoint. A consequence used constantly: if T intertwines two normal operators then the ranges and kernels respecting one spectral projection respect the other, so T intertwines their spectral measures; in particular a normal operator commuting with T has a reducing subspace structure compatible with T.
NORMALITY of both M and N is essential;
for general operators the conclusion is false.
T need not be normal, invertible, or anything but bounded.
The boundedness of F, which Liouville needs, is exactly where normality enters through the unitarity of those exponential factors.

P0013.title: Attempt on Expected Lovasz theta of a dense independent-edge graph
P0013.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Complement symmetry and uniform-integrability obstruction Result: The theta product inequality theta(G) theta(complement G)>=n and complement symmetry of G(n,1/2) give E theta>=sqrt(n) by arithmetic-geometric mean. A proof of concentration on a logarithmic scale would still need tail control: set Z_n to plus or minus (log n)/2, each with probability 1/(2 sqrt(n)), and zero otherwise. Then Z_n tends to zero in probability and variance, but E exp(Z_n) tends to 3/2. Check: The example has a symmetric law and exp(Z_n) in [n^(-1/2),n^(1/2)]. Its expectation is 1-1/sqrt(n)+(1+n^(-1))/(2), which tends to 3/2. It is not a random-graph construction. Obstruction: Need a sharp upper bound and uniform integrability at the sqrt(n) scale; complement symmetry only yields the lower bound.

C0003.title: Attempt on Bypassing the Laplace-transform tail condition for the DGFF extremal measure
C0003.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Try to derive the tail exponent from the Gibbs-Markov fixed-point equation as for smoothing transforms (Durrett-Liggett classification). Result: The Gibbs-Markov property along dyadic square partitions gives a fixed-point equation of smoothing type Z^D =_d sum_i e^{alpha Phi_i} Z^{D_i} with Gaussian binding field Phi and 4 pieces; Durrett-Liggett gives, for such equations, that non-trivial solutions have tails whose exponent is the root of a structure equation, here forcing E[Z^D(A)^s] finite iff s < 1. This yields the correct tail EXPONENT (P(Z^D(A) > t) decays like t^{-1} up to slowly varying factors) but not the precise Laplace asymptotic E e^{-lambda Z} = 1 - c lambda log(1/lambda)(1+o(1)) demanded by property (5); the slowly varying factor is exactly the content of the conjecture and the Durrett-Liggett theory does not fix it. Obstruction: Smoothing-transform theory fixes the power in the tail but not the logarithmic correction; the log factor is what (5) asserts.

C0060.title: Attempt on Positivity of the vacant-set threshold u* for random interlacements on the Sierpinski gasket times Z
C0060.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Try the renormalisation argument for u* > 0 with the gasket's polynomial growth and heat-kernel bounds. Result: The Z^d proof of u* > 0 (Sznitman) uses a renormalisation over boxes at scales L_n with the decoupling of the interlacement in distant boxes controlled by the capacity of boxes (order L^{d-2}) against the volume of the sprinkling; on G x Z the walk has spectral dimension d_s = 2 log 3 / log 5 + 1 = 2.365 and walk dimension d_w = log 5 / log 2 = 2.32 in G, and the capacity of a box of side L in G x Z is of order L^{d_f + 1 - d_w} with d_f = log 3/log 2 = 1.585, i.e. L^{0.26}: capacity grows very slowly. The renormalisation needs the number of boxes at scale L_{n+1} covering a box at scale L_n times the probability that interlacement at level u hits a box (about u cap(box)) to be summable; with capacity L^{0.26} and the gasket's self-similar structure one needs the box at scale L_n to be avoided by the vacant-set-crossing with probability decaying faster than the branching of the renormalisation, which fails because the exponent 0.26 is too small to dominate the combinatorial factor of the gasket's cut sets: a crossing of a gasket triangle can be blocked by hitting one of only three corner regions (the gasket has cut points), so the vacant set is blocked whenever the interlacement hits the three corner neighbourhoods, which at level u happens with probability roughly 1 - exp(-3u cap(corner region)) -> a constant not tending to zero as the scale grows only if cap(corner region) stays bounded; since cap grows like L^{0.26} it tends to infinity and the blocking probability tends to 1. This argues for u* = 0 on G x Z: at any u > 0, at large scales every corner region is hit and the gasket's cut-point structure disconnects the vacant set. The argument is heuristic because the corner regions of the Z-direction are cylinders, not points, and a vacant path can bypass a corner through the Z direction; the honest conclusion is that the answer hinges on whether the Z direction provides bypasses of the gasket's cut points, which I could not settle. Key identity: Capacity of a box of side L in G x Z is about L^{0.26}; the gasket's cut points force vacant crossings through corner regions whose hitting probability tends to 1. Obstruction: The Z-direction bypass of gasket cut points is not quantified; the sign of the answer is unclear.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0060-positivity-of-the-vacant-set-threshold-u-for-random-interlacements-on

C0085.title: Attempt on Two-point function of high-dimensional invasion percolation
C0085.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compare the invasion cluster two-point function with the IIC two-point function and locate the difference. Result: The IIC two-point function P_IIC(x in cluster) is asymptotic to A' |x|^{-(d-4)} in high dimensions (from the lace expansion of the IIC, Hofstad-Jarai), and the invasion percolation cluster is expected to have the same decay exponent because the invasion cluster near infinity looks like a critical cluster with a slightly supercritical 'ponds' structure at scales below the current pond size. The source notes that the IIC and IPC have different scaling limits on the tree (Angel-Goodman-den Hollander-Slade), so the constants A and A' differ and the exponent may agree. A rigorous bound: since the invasion cluster contains the IIC-like structure... no inclusion holds in either direction. The ponds structure: invasion percolation on Z^d invades the cluster of the origin at level p_c + eps_k where eps_k decreases to 0 along the pond sequence; the probability that x at distance r is invaded is roughly the probability that x lies in the p_c + eps(r) cluster of the origin restricted to the ball of radius r, with eps(r) the level at scale r; in high dimensions eps(r) ~ r^{-2} (mean-field correlation length exponent 1/2), and P_{p_c + r^{-2}}(0 <-> x, |x| = r) is of order r^{-(d-2)} times the number of extra connections... a computation via the slightly supercritical two-point function gives P(x in IPC) ~ r^{-(d-2)} x (number of vertices at distance about r in the cluster)/... I could not make this precise; the mean-field prediction of the exponent d-4 comes from the IIC analogy. Not resolved; the reduction is to a slightly supercritical two-point function estimate at p_c + r^{-2} with matching constants, which is a Problem 11.1-type supercritical quantity. Obstruction: Requires slightly supercritical two-point asymptotics with constants (C0065-type input).

C0131.title: Attempt on Recurrence-transience dichotomy for excited random walks in dimension d >= 2
C0131.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compare with the RWRE 0-1 law in d >= 3 (C0044) and locate the extra difficulty from self-interaction. Result: For Markovian RWRE the dichotomy question is the directional 0-1 law (C0044, open in d >= 3). For excited random walks the process is not Markov, and even the statement 'either recurrent or transient' (return to the origin infinitely often a.s. or finitely often a.s.) is not implied by any Markov-chain dichotomy; the source's Definition 3.1 asks for a 0-1 law for the number of returns. A route: the event {X returns to 0 infinitely often} is determined by the walk in the environment, and by the ergodicity of the environment its probability does not depend on the starting point in the sense P_x(return to x i.o.) is constant in x; but P_0(return to 0 i.o.) in (0,1) is not excluded by that. The Kalikow-type argument for RWRE (P_0(A_l union A_{-l}) in {0,1}) uses that the walk from 0 and from a far point in the same environment can be coupled after a hitting event; for excited walks the coupled walks see different cookie states (one walk has eaten cookies), which is the extra difficulty. Under (UEL) and boundedness of the stacks (M cookies per site), a walk that has visited a region changes the environment there in a bounded way, and once the walk leaves a region for good the modified cookies are irrelevant; so for transient behaviour the modification is harmless, while recurrence requires infinitely many returns through modified regions. I could not produce a proof; the sharpest statement I can defend: if the excited walk is transient in the sense |X_n| -> infinity with positive probability, then, under (IID) and (UEL), it is transient a.s., by the following argument: on the event of transience the walk eventually leaves every ball, and the environment outside any ball is untouched and i.i.d., so the probability of transience given the walk is at distance R from the origin at a time after which it never returns to the ball... this does not close either because the walk's future depends on the eaten cookies inside the ball only if it returns. Recorded as attempted without result. Obstruction: Self-interaction breaks the coupling arguments behind Markovian 0-1 laws.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0131-recurrence-transience-dichotomy-for-excited-random-walks-in-dimension

P0016.title: Attempt on Worst square-submatrix conditioning in a Gaussian frame
P0016.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Union small-ball lower bound and one-normal upper bound Result: For a standard M-by-M real Gaussian matrix A, sigma_min(A)<=t implies that some column has distance at most sqrt(M)t from the span of the other columns: project a minimizing unit vector equation using a coordinate of magnitude at least 1/sqrt(M). Each such distance has the law |N(0,1)|, so P(sigma_min<=t)<=sqrt(2/pi) M^(3/2)t. There are at most 4^M M-row submatrices of a (2M-1)-by-M frame. Therefore its minimum omega exceeds exp(-(log 4+epsilon)M) with probability tending to one. Conversely fix M-1 rows and a unit normal u. The M remaining row projections are independent N(0,1), and omega is at most their minimum absolute value, giving omega<=C log(M)/M with probability tending to one for sufficiently large C. Check: Full spark holds almost surely. Adding rows increases the Gram matrix, so the minimum relevant frame bound is attained among M-row subsets. Both bounds use union/inclusion inequalities and never assume independence among overlapping minors. Obstruction: The exponential lower bound and polynomial upper bound are far apart. Sharp extremes of the strongly dependent minors remain uncontrolled.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0016-worst-square-submatrix-conditioning-in-a-gaussian-frame

P0046.title: Attempt on Connecting a free uniform spanning forest by arbitrarily sparse invariant additions
P0046.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Connection to the cost equality obstruction Result: If the free forest is already connected, taking its own configuration gives the requested extension with no added edges. Otherwise, an invariant connected extension with each edge added with probability at most epsilon would have expected root degree at most E deg_F(o)+deg_G(o) epsilon. The standard invariant-graphing bound would then imply cost(Gamma)<=E deg_F(o)/2=1+beta_1(Gamma) after epsilon tends to zero. Check: The root-degree estimate is the finite sum of per-edge addition probabilities. Combined with the known opposite cost inequality, the proposed construction would prove equality, not merely a weak approximation statement. Obstruction: No dependent sprinkling construction was found. This reduction explains why independent sprinkling or a generic connectivity argument does not settle the question.
